title: The tax the political class sets aside for itself
intro: Companies have been banned from donating to campaigns since 2015. Today the taxpayer pays for them, through two funds written into law: the Party Fund, which runs every year, and the Electoral Fund, which appears in election years. In 2026 the two together come to more than R$ 6 billion.
total.label: is what the two funds add up to in the 2026 budget
total.note: The 2026 Electoral Fund is R$ 4,961,519,777.00, split between 30 parties. The Party Fund is estimated at R$ 1.4 billion in the budget law — in 2025 it passed R$ 1,126,071,496.13 to 19 parties, plus R$ 102,572,513.68 coming from electoral fines.
raise.title: Congress quintupled its own fund, and said where it would come from
raise.body: On 30 September 2025 the Joint Budget Committee raised the amount reserved in the 2026 budget for the elections from R$ 1 billion to R$ 4.9 billion. The money did not come from nowhere: the government had already taken R$ 1 billion from state-bench parliamentary amendments, and the committee took another R$ 2.9 billion from the same amendments. The rest came out of non-mandatory spending. The reserve for bench amendments fell from R$ 15.2 billion to R$ 11.2 billion.
parties.title: How much each party gets from the 2026 Electoral Fund
parties.note: The split follows representation in Congress: the more members of parliament, the more money. The top three parties take almost 40% of the total. The list below has the 21 parties the Senate news agency published; there are 30 in all.
question: Companies cannot fund campaigns, and the taxpayer was never asked. That is R$ 6 billion of tax money in an election year, taken partly from the amendments that would have funded works in the states. Did anyone vote for this?
